summary: Provides the obsoleted IPv6-specific MIB modules so repositories can be updated, noting that newer IP-MIB, TCP-MIB, UDP-MIB and IP-FORWARD-MIB handle both IPv4 and IPv6.

eli5.summary: Old IPv6-only monitoring lists are saved for reference because newer shared lists cover both versions.

questions: why were rfc 2465 and 2466 made historic
subtitle: Republishing the old IPv6-only MIB modules, marked obsolete, so MIB repositories stop presenting them as current.

tldr.problem: Updated IP-MIB, UDP-MIB, TCP-MIB and IP-FORWARD-MIB modules handle IPv4 and IPv6 together, but MIB repositories still held the old IPv6-only modules unchanged, which left an unclear situation.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC republishes IPV6-TC, IPV6-MIB, IPV6-ICMP-MIB, IPV6-UDP-MIB and IPV6-TCP-MIB with every object's status changed to obsolete, and reclassifies the four RFCs that held them as Historic.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8096 obsoletes RFC 2452, RFC 2454, RFC 2465 and RFC 2466. Implementers should use the combined IPv4/IPv6 MIB modules instead.

today: RFC 8096 is Informational. It obsoletes RFC 2452, RFC 2454, RFC 2465 and RFC 2466, which it reclassifies as Historic, and no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why the Old IPv6 MIBs Were Republished
sections.content:
In 2005 and 2006 the IPv6 MIB update group published new versions of the IP-MIB (RFC 4293), UDP-MIB (RFC 4113), TCP-MIB (RFC 4022) and IP-FORWARD-MIB (RFC 4292). These use the InetAddressType/InetAddress construct to handle IPv4 and IPv6 in the same table.

The RFC Editor marked these documents as obsoleting the matching IPv6-only MIBs. But the extracted MIB content in repositories never changed, and the original RFCs stayed at Proposed Standard, as is normal IETF policy. People often overlook that the later revisions of the original modules added IPv6 support.

RFC 8096 therefore republishes the old modules with the Structure of Management Information (SMI) status changed to obsolete. The RFC calls this an unusual step and not the intended path for every obsolete MIB module.
sections.eli5: The old IPv6-only lists were replaced by better lists, but nobody had crossed the old ones off. This document crosses them off clearly.

sections.title: The Five Obsolete Modules
sections.content:
Sections 2 to 6 reproduce the old modules as Historic: IPV6-TC (textual conventions), IPV6-MIB (the general IPv6 group, with interface, address, route and neighbor tables), IPV6-ICMP-MIB, IPV6-UDP-MIB and IPV6-TCP-MIB. Together they take up most of the document, and the explanatory text is only a few pages.

Each object has STATUS obsolete, and its description says what replaces it. The text of the modules is otherwise old content, so the useful parts of the RFC are those replacement pointers. For example, ipv6Interfaces has no direct replacement, but its value can be derived from the number of rows in the IP-MIB ipv6InterfaceTable.
sections.eli5: It is like keeping old phone books on a shelf with a big sticker on each saying 'out of date, use the new one'.

sections.title: Where the Old Objects Went
sections.content:
The descriptions in the republished modules name the replacements. The IPv6-specific address and interface-index types are obsoleted by INET-ADDRESS-MIB::InetAddress and IF-MIB::InterfaceIndex. The forwarding switch ipv6Forwarding is replaced by IP-MIB::ipv6IpForwarding, and ipv6DefaultHopLimit by IP-MIB::ipv6IpDefaultHopLimit.

The old interface table ipv6IfTable is replaced by IP-MIB::ipv6InterfaceTable. Several of its columns point to the generic interfaces MIB, such as IF-MIB::ifDescr and IF-MIB::ifPhysAddress. The lower-layer relationship that ipv6IfLowerLayer expressed can be expressed with the IF-STACK-TABLE. The TCP group is obsoleted by several groups in TCP-MIB.
sections.eli5: Each crossed-out entry has a note on it that tells you which new entry to look at instead.

sections.title: Reclassification to Historic
sections.content: The document reclassifies RFC 2452, RFC 2454, RFC 2465 and RFC 2466 to Historic. These are the RFCs that originally contained the IPv6 TCP, UDP, general and textual-convention, and ICMPv6 MIB modules, and RFC 8096 obsoletes all four.
sections.eli5: The four old books are moved from the 'use this' shelf to the 'history' shelf.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content:
IANA updated the SMI Numbers registry. In the Internet-standard MIB section it removed RFC 1213 as a reference for icmp (mib-2.5) and udp (mib-2.7), pointed tcp (mib-2.6) at RFC 4022, and removed RFC 2012 as a reference for tcpMIB (mib-2.49).

It added a "(Historic)" annotation for ipv6MIB (mib-2.55) and ipv6IcmpMIB (mib-2.56), and for the experimental entry 74 ("IPv6 MIB"). It changed the "(Historical)" annotation for experimental.87 ("ipv6UdpMIB") to "(Historic)" and pointed experimental.86 and experimental.87 at this document.
sections.eli5: The big public list of assigned numbers got matching notes, so everyone can see which entries are old.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document contains only obsolete objects. RFC 2578 says such objects "should not be implemented and/or can be removed if previously implemented". The RFC therefore concludes that it has no security implications. If an implementation had any security issue from these objects, removing them would improve its security.
sections.eli5: Nobody should use these old lists, so they cannot cause trouble. Throwing them away is the safest choice.
